Q1MCQXOR Regions

Lecture wala XOR network (hidden $h_1$: OR-type, threshold $0.5$; hidden $h_2$: NAND-type, threshold $-1.5$; output AND, threshold $1.5$) input space ko kitne regions me divide karta hai?

  • ✓a. 2
  • b. 4
  • c. 6
  • d. 8
Solution kholo
  1. $h_1 = 1$ iff $x_1 + x_2 \ge 0.5$ (OR)
    $h_2 = 1$ iff $-x_1 - x_2 \ge -1.5$ ⇔ $x_1+x_2 \le 1.5$ (NAND)
    $y = 1$ iff $h_1 + h_2 \ge 1.5$.
  2. To $y = 1 \iff 0.5 \le x_1 + x_2 \le 1.5$ — do parallel lines ke beech ka diagonal strip.
  3. Classification-wise space 2 regions me banta hai: positive region (strip — $(0,1)$ aur $(1,0)$ isi me) aur negative region (baaki sab — $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$).

Answer: a — 2 regions

Q2MCQLayer Counting

Ek chain network: inputs $x_1, x_2$ → neuron (0.5) → neuron (0.5) → neuron (0.5) → output $y$. Kitne hidden layers hain?

  • a. 1
  • ✓b. 2
  • c. 3
  • d. 4
Solution kholo
  1. Input aur output ke beech jo neuron-layers hain wahi hidden layers hain.
  2. Pehla (0.5) neuron = hidden layer 1
    dusra = hidden layer 2
    teesra (0.5) neuron output layer hai jo $y$ de raha hai.
  3. Input layer ko hidden count me kabhi mat lena.

Answer: b — 2 hidden layers (Bhai bas beech ke neurons gino — input layer ko hidden count me lena hi mat.)

Q3MCQMinimum Neurons

Decision boundary di hai: do parallel diagonal lines — dono ke bahar wale regions green (positive: points A, D) aur beech ki strip white (negative: points B, C). Aisi boundary ke liye minimum kitne neurons chahiye?

  • a. 1
  • b. 2
  • ✓c. 3
  • d. 4
  • e. 5
Solution kholo
  1. Positive region = do half-planes ka union — ye XOR-type layout hai (A, D positive; B, C negative).
  2. Ek perceptron = ek seedhi line. 2 neurons se bhi ye "dono taraf positive" region nahi banta.
  3. Construction: hidden neuron 1 → ek half-plane, hidden neuron 2 → dusra half-plane, output neuron → un dono ka OR. Total = 2 hidden + 1 output = 3.

Answer: c — 3 neurons

Q4Multiple Select2¹⁰²⁴ Functions

MLP: input layer + 1 hidden layer (1024 perceptrons) + output layer (1 perceptron). Kaunse statements true hain?

  • ✓a. Network $2^{1024}$ Boolean functions implement kar sakta hai
  • b. Network $2^{10}$ Boolean functions implement kar sakta hai
  • c. Har hidden perceptron sirf 10 Boolean inputs le sakta hai
Solution kholo
  1. Representation power result: hidden layer ke $N$ perceptrons wala network $2^{N}$ boolean functions implement karta hai (output neuron kaunse hidden detectors ko "on" karta hai, ye $2^N$ combinations hain).
  2. $N = 1024$ → $2^{1024}$ functions → (a) ✓, (b) ✗.
  3. (c) ✗ — perceptron real-valued inputs le sakta hai.
    Boolean-only restriction nahi hai.

Answer: a (note: is question me official PDF me tick print nahi hua tha — answer printed explanation se verified hai)

Q5MCQSigmoid Plot

Sigmoid function $\sigma(x) = 1/(1 + e^{-x+2})$ ke liye kaunsa plot sahi hai?

  • a. Centered sigmoid — $0.5$ crossing at $x = 0$
  • ✓b. Right-shifted sigmoid — positive slope, $0.5$ crossing at $x = +2$
Solution kholo
  1. $\sigma(x) = 0.5$ exactly tab jab exponent zero ho: $-x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$.
  2. General form se: $w = 1, b = -2$ — positive slope, aur $b$ negative hone se curve right shift hua hai (crossing $-b/w = +2$).
  3. $x \to -\infty$ pe $\sigma \to 0$ aur $x \to +\infty$ pe $\sigma \to 1$ — standard S-shape.

Answer: b — crossing at x = +2

Q6Short AnswerFit w

Sigmoid $\sigma(x) = 1/(1+e^{-(wx+b)})$ ko do points se fit karna hai: $x_1 \approx (-0.4,\ 0.12)$ aur $x_2 \approx (0.2,\ 0.98)$. $w$ ki value kya hogi?

Solution kholo
  1. Sigmoid $0.5$ ki value tabhi leta hai jab $wx + b = 0$, yaani crossing point $x = -b/w$.
  2. Do points ko join karne wali chord $y = 0.5$ line ko $x \approx -0.2$ pe kaat-ti hai (points ke beech ka midpoint-ish) → $-b/w = -0.2$ → $b/w = 0.2$.
  3. Dono points se exact fit karne par solution aata hai: $w = 10$, $b = 2$ (jo $b/w = 0.2$ bhi satisfy karta hai).
  4. Verify:
    $\sigma(-0.4) = 1/(1+e^{-(-4+2)}) = 1/(1+e^{2}) \approx 0.119$ ✓
    $\sigma(0.2) = 1/(1+e^{-(2+2)}) = 1/(1+e^{-4}) \approx 0.982$ ✓

Answer: w = 10 (Dekh bhai — 0.5-crossing wala ek formula, aur kaam khatam.)

Q7Short AnswerFit b

Usi hi setup (Q6) me $b$ ki value kya hogi?

Solution kholo
  1. Q6 se: crossing condition $b/w = 0.2$.
  2. $w = 10$ use karo → $b = 0.2 \times 10 = 2$.
  3. Check: $\sigma(-0.2) = 1/(1+e^{0}) = 0.5$ ✓ — curve exactly beech me cross kar rahi hai.

Answer: b = 2

Q8Multiple SelectSigmoid Properties

$\sigma(z) = 1/(1+e^{-z})$ ke liye kaunse statements true hain?

  • ✓a. Continuously differentiable hai
  • ✓b. Monotonic hai
  • c. Maximum $z \to -\infty$ pe attain karti hai
  • ✓d. 0 aur 1 ke beech bounded hai
Solution kholo
  1. (a) ✓ $\sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)(1-\sigma(z))$ — continuous, har jagah exist karti hai.
  2. (b) ✓ $\sigma'(z) \gt 0$ hamesha → monotonically increasing.
  3. (c) ✗ $z \to -\infty$ pe $\sigma \to 0$ — ye minimum hai, maximum nahi! (supremum 1 $+\infty$ pe aata hai.)
  4. (d) ✓ Finite $z$ ke liye $0 \lt \sigma(z) \lt 1$.

Answer: a, b, d

Q9MCQTaylor Types

Taylor expansion me $\mathcal{L}(\theta)$, $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}(\theta)$ aur $\nabla_\theta^2 \mathcal{L}(\theta)$ — in shapes ka sahi order kya hai?

$$\mathcal{L}(\theta + \eta u) = \mathcal{L}(\theta) + \eta u^T \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}(\theta) + \frac{\eta^2}{2!}u^T \nabla_\theta^2 \mathcal{L}(\theta)u + \cdots$$
  • a. vector, vector, vector
  • b. vector, scalar, matrix
  • c. scalar, scalar, scalar
  • ✓d. scalar, vector, matrix
Solution kholo
  1. $\mathcal{L}(\theta)$ = single number → scalar.
  2. $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}$ = first-order partials ka vector (har parameter ke liye ek) → vector (gradient).
  3. $\nabla_\theta^2 \mathcal{L}$ = second-order partials ki $d \times d$ table → matrix (Hessian).
  4. Sanity check: $u^T(\text{vector})$ = scalar ✓, $u^T(\text{matrix})u$ = scalar ✓ — terms ka dimension consistent hai.

Answer: d — scalar, vector, matrix (Scalar → vector → matrix — bas ye teen words yaad rakho, aisi har question 10 second me hogi.)

Q10Short AnswerGD Iterations

$f(w) = 0.1w^2 + w - 1$ ka minimum GD se dhundhna hai: $w_0 = 10$, $\eta = 0.5$. Teen updates ke baad $w$ ki value?

Solution kholo
  1. $f'(w) = 0.2w + 1$
    update: $w \leftarrow w - 0.5 f'(w)$.
  2. Update 1: $f'(10) = 3$ → $w_1 = 10 - 1.5 = 8.5$
  3. Update 2: $f'(8.5) = 2.7$ → $w_2 = 8.5 - 1.35 = 7.15$
  4. Update 3: $f'(7.15) = 2.43$ → $w_3 = 7.15 - 1.215 = 5.935$
  5. Sanity: true minimum $w = -5$ hai.
    $w$ monotonically ghat raha hai uski taraf — track sahi hai.

Answer: w ≈ 5.93 (official PDF ke explanation me ek arithmetic slip hai — 0.2·8.5+1 = 2.7 hai, 2.8 nahi; exact answer 5.935 = printed "5.93")

Q11MCQFunction Combination

Teen functions ki plots di hain: $f$ = step jo $x \approx 0.75$ pe jump karti hai; $g$ = step jo $x \approx 0.5$ pe jump karti hai; $h$ = rectangular pulse (height ≈ 0.5) jo $0.5$ se $0.75$ ke beech hai. Sahi combination?

  • a. $h = f - g$
  • b. $h = 0.5*(f+g)$
  • ✓c. $h = 0.5*(g-f)$
  • d. $h = 0.5*(f-g)$
Solution kholo
  1. Interval $(0.5, 0.75)$ me: $g = 1$ (pehle jump hui) aur $f = 0$ (abhi tak jump nahi hui) → $g - f = 1$.
  2. Baaki sab jagah dono equal → $g - f = 0$. To $0.5(g-f)$ = exactly wahi pulse!
  3. Baaki options check: (a) $-1$ ka pulse, (b) staircase $0 \to 0.5 \to 1$ (wapas 0 nahi girta), (d) negative pulse. Sirf (c) match karta hai.

Answer: c — h = 0.5*(g−f) (ye wahi pattern hai jo Week 2 ke tower construction me use hota hai — do shifted sigmoids ka difference!)

✎ W2 PA se kya seekhna hai

XOR-network = 2 regions; hidden layers gin-te waqt input ko count mat karo; $2^N$ functions from $N$ hidden neurons; sigmoid crossing $x = -b/w$; scalar→vector→matrix Taylor order; GD iterations me naya $w$ har step use hota hai; aur shifted steps ka difference = pulse/tower. Done!

Part 03 · Week 3

Feedforward Networks & Backpropagation

Architecture, Output Functions & Loss Functions, Backpropagation ki poori derivation — intuition se lekar pseudocode tak.

≈ 75 min readSource: Lecture 4 notesLevel: Zero se

Dekh bhai, Week 3 ka naam bada lagta hai, par kaam chhota hai: neurons ko layers me stack karo, loss choose karo, aur chain rule se gradients nikaalo. Backprop ka poora khel bas chain rule hai — bas thoda organized tareeke se lagana hai.

3.1Feedforward Neural Network — Architecture

Ab hum single neurons se aage badh kar multilayered network of neurons — yaani Feedforward Neural Network (FFNN) — banate hain. Structure yaad rakho:

  • Input: $n$-dimensional vector $x$ — ise layer-0 ($0$-th layer) bolo.
  • Hidden layers: $L-1$ layers, har ek me $n$ neurons (example me).
  • Output layer: $k$ neurons ($k$ classes ke liye) — ise $(L)$-th layer bolo. Total $L+1$ levels hain (0 se L tak).

Core Equations — Inhe Kanthasth Kar Lo

Layer $i$ ke liye (simplify karke $a_i(x)$ ko $a_i$ likhte hain):

$$a_i = b_i + W_i h_{i-1} \qquad\qquad h_i = g(a_i)$$
  • $W_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, $b_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ — layer $i-1$ se $i$ tak ke weights/bias (0 < i < L)
  • $W_L \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$, $b_L \in \mathbb{R}^k$ — last hidden layer se output tak
  • $g$ = activation function (logistic, tanh, linear, ReLU…)
  • Output layer: $f(x) = h_L = O(a_L)$ — jahan $O$ = output activation (softmax, linear…)

Poora network ek expanded form me:

$$\hat{y}_i = f(x_i) = O\Big(W_3\, g\big(W_2\, g(W_1 x + b_1) + b_2\big) + b_3\Big) \quad (L = 3 \text{ ke liye})$$
ML SetupFFNN case
Data$\{x_i, y_i\}_{i=1}^{N}$
Model$\hat{y} = O(W_L g(\cdots g(W_1 x + b_1)\cdots) + b_L)$
Parameters$\theta = [W_1, \ldots, W_L, b_1, \ldots, b_L]$
Objective$\min_\theta\ L(\theta)$ — e.g. $\frac{1}{N}\sum_i \sum_j (\hat{y}_{ij} - y_{ij})^2$
AlgorithmGradient Descent with Backpropagation (aane wala hai!)

3.2Output Functions aur Loss Functions — Kaunsa Kab?

Do sawal hain jo solve karne hain:
(1) Loss function $L(\theta)$ kaise choose karein?
(2) Gradient $\nabla_\theta$ kaise compute karein?
Pehla sawal problem ki nature pe depend karta hai — do classic cases dekho.

Case 1: Real-valued output (Regression) → Linear + Squared Error

Movie ratings predict karni hain: $y_j \in \mathbb{R}^3$ (IMDb, Critics, RT ratings — jaise $[7.5, 8.2, 7.7]$). Loss squared error se deviation capture hota hai:

$$L(\theta) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\left(\hat{y}_{ij} - y_{ij}\right)^2$$

Ab dhyan do: kya output activation $O$ ko logistic rakh sakte hain? Nahi! Logistic output ko 0 aur 1 ke beech bound kar deta hai, jabki humein $\hat{y}_j \in \mathbb{R}$ chahiye (rating 8.2 kaise milegi?). Isliye yahan $O$ = linear function:

$$\hat{y} = h_L = O(a_L) = W_L a_L + b_L \quad\text{(ab } \hat{y} \text{ 0-1 me bounded nahi hai)}$$

Case 2: Classification (k classes) → Softmax + Cross-Entropy

Ab image ko $k$ classes me classify karna hai (Apple/Mango/Orange/Banana). True label one-hot vector hai: $y = [1, 0, 0, 0]$ — notice ki $y$ ek probability distribution hai (sums to 1)! To logical requirement: $\hat{y}$ bhi probability distribution hona chahiye. Kaunsa $O$ ye guarantee karega?

✦ Softmax Function $$\hat{y}_j = O(a_L)_j = \frac{e^{a_{L,j}}}{\sum_{i=1}^{k} e^{a_{L,i}}}$$

Properties: har entry $(0,1)$ me, aur saari entries ka sum = 1 — perfect probability distribution! $a_{L,j}$ bada → us class ki probability badi. Isi softmax + cross-entropy combo pe hum poora backprop derive karenge.

Ab dono probability distributions ($y$ aur $\hat{y}$) ke beech ka "difference" kaise naape? Jawaab: Cross-entropy:

$$L(\theta) = -\sum_{c=1}^{k} y_c \log \hat{y}_c$$

Kyunki $y_c = 1$ sirf true class $\ell$ ke liye aur 0 baaki sab ke liye, ye simplify ho jata hai:

$$L(\theta) = -\log \hat{y}_\ell$$

Interpretation: $\hat{y}_\ell$ = probability ki input $x$, class $\ell$ me hai. Loss kehta hai — "is probability ko 1 ke jitna paas le jao". Aur $-\log \hat{y}_\ell$ ko log-likelihood kehte hain — minimize cross-entropy = maximize likelihood of data. (Bonus: MSE bhi technically classification me use ho sakta hai one-hot targets ke saath, par CE standard aur better hai — W3 PA Q4 me isi pe question tha!)

3.3Backpropagation — Intuition (Zimmevari ka Khel)

Gradient Descent ke liye humein $\nabla_\theta L(\theta)$ chahiye — jisme $\nabla_{W_1}, \ldots, \nabla_{W_L}, \nabla_{b_1}, \ldots, \nabla_{b_L}$ sab shamil hain. Ye "nasty" gradient kaise nikale? Backpropagation ka intuition ek kahani hai — zimmevari (responsibility) ki kahani.

Concept kaafi simple hai bhai, naam se darr mat lagao — bas har layer se poochna hai "is galti me tera kitna hissa hai?" Wahi hissa hi gradient ban jata hai. Question me bhi bas yehi lagana hai.

❝ Story Mode — Loss Aaya To Kaun Zimmedar?

Output pe loss aaya: $-\log\hat{y}_\ell$. Ab pata karna hai ki is loss ke liye kaun kaun zimmedar hai.

Hum output layer se kehte hain: "Oi! Sahi output nahi de raha ho, zimmevari lo!" Output layer kehta hai: "Thik hai, apni hisse ki zimmevari leta hoon… par samajh jao, main utna hi accha hoon jitna mujhse neeche wala hidden layer aur weights hain — aakhir $\hat{y} = O(W_L h_{L-1} + b_L)$ hai."

Ab hum $W_L, b_L, h_{L-1}$ se poochte hain: "kya problem hai tumme?" $W_L$ aur $b_L$ apni zimmevari le lete hain, par kehte hain "hum utne hi acche hain jitna pre-activation $a_L$ hai." Pre-activation kehta hai: "main to sirf utna accha hoon jitna neeche wala hidden layer aur weights hain."

Aise hi ye zimmevari ka silsila layer-by-layer neeche tak chalta hai, aur hum realize karte hain ki zimmevari saare weights aur biases ki hai. Par unse seedha baat karne ki jagah layers ke through baat karna easier hai — aur yehi chain rule karta hai!

Deep-but-thin network pe chain rule dekho (har layer me 1 neuron — $x_1 \to a_{11} \to h_{11} \to a_{21} \to h_{21} \to \cdots \to a_{L1} \to \hat{y}$):

$$\frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial W_{111}} = \frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial \hat{y}}\cdot\frac{\partial \hat{y}}{\partial a_{L11}}\cdot\frac{\partial a_{L11}}{\partial h_{21}}\cdot\frac{\partial h_{21}}{\partial a_{21}}\cdot\frac{\partial a_{21}}{\partial h_{11}}\cdot\frac{\partial h_{11}}{\partial a_{11}}\cdot\frac{\partial a_{11}}{\partial W_{111}}$$

Isko "compress" karke 4 hisson me dekho — ye hi roadmap hai:

$$\frac{\partial L}{\partial W_{111}} = \underbrace{\frac{\partial L}{\partial h_{11}}}_{\text{layer se poocho}} \cdot \underbrace{\frac{\partial h_{11}}{\partial W_{111}}}_{\text{weight se poocho}}$$

Aur $\frac{\partial L}{\partial h_{11}}$ ko aage toda ja sakta hai — upstream gradients ka use. Ab formally teen "quantities of interest" hain:

#QuantityMatlab
1$\nabla_{a_L} L(\theta)$Output units ke pre-activation ka gradient
2$\nabla_{h_i} L(\theta),\ \nabla_{a_i} L(\theta)$Hidden layers ke gradients ($1 \le i \lt L$)
3$\nabla_{W_k} L(\theta),\ \nabla_{b_k} L(\theta)$Weights aur biases ke gradients

3.4Gradient w.r.t. Output Units — Step 1

Focus: cross-entropy loss + softmax output. Pehle loss ko $\hat{y}_i$ ke respect me differentiate karo.

$$L(\theta) = -\log \hat{y}_\ell \quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial \hat{y}_i} = \begin{cases} -\dfrac{1}{\hat{y}_\ell}, & i = \ell \ \text{(true class)} \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

Vector form me — $e^{(\ell)}$ one-hot vector use karke (jiska $\ell$-th element 1 hai, baaki 0):

$$\nabla_{\hat{y}} L(\theta) = -\frac{1}{\hat{y}_\ell} e^{(\ell)}$$

Par humein asli mein chahiye $\nabla_{a_L} L$ — kyunki softmax ke baad chain aage $a_L$ se connect hoti hai. Softmax ka derivative: $\hat{y}_i = \frac{e^{a_{L,i}}}{\sum_{i'} e^{a_{L,i'}}}$, aur quotient rule + quotient-differentiation shortcut ($\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\frac{g(x)}{h(x)} = \frac{g'(x)h(x) - g(x)h'(x)}{h(x)^2}$) lagane par:

$$\frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial a_{L,i}} = -(1 - \mathbb{1}_{(\ell = i)})\,\hat{y}_i$$

Iska detailed unroll (jaisa slides me hai): $-\frac{\partial \log \hat{y}_\ell}{\partial a_{L,i}} = -\frac{1}{\hat{y}_\ell}\cdot\frac{\partial \hat{y}_\ell}{\partial a_{L,i}}$ — aur $\hat{y}_\ell$ ka $a_{L,i}$ ke respect me derivative softmax ki classic property se $(\hat{y}_\ell \mathbb{1}_{(\ell=i)} - \hat{y}_\ell \hat{y}_i)$ aata hai. Poora vector:

✦ Yaad Rakho — Sabse Sundar Result of Backprop $$\nabla_{a_L} L(\theta) = -\left(e^{(\ell)} - \hat{y}\right) = \hat{y} - e^{(\ell)}$$

Matlab output layer ka gradient = predicted probabilities minus true one-hot label. No messy softmax-Jacobian, no $1/\hat{y}$ — sirf ek simple subtraction! Isi "shortcut" ki wajah se softmax + cross-entropy ka combo itna popular hai. Quiz 2 Q17 me direct use hua: $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial a_{L,\ell} = \hat{y}_\ell - 1 = 0.99 - 1 = -0.01$.

◈ Samajh — $\hat{y} - y$ Kyun Itna Elegant Hai

Agar model sahi class ko 0.99 probability de raha hai ($\hat{y}_\ell = 0.99$), to error signal sirf $-0.01$ — "bas thoda sa push aur". Agar galat confidence ke saath 0.01 de raha hai, to error signal $-0.99$ — "bade bade corrections karo!". Loss khud decide karta hai ki kitna tez seekhna hai. Yehi adaptive behaviour squared error me itna clean nahi milta.

3.5Gradient w.r.t. Hidden Units — Step 2

Ab hidden units ke gradients. Pehle ek chhota sa chain rule upgrade: agar $p(z)$ kai intermediate functions $q_m(z)$ ke through $z$ pe depend karta hai, to saare paths pe sum karna hota hai:

$$\frac{\partial p(z)}{\partial z} = \sum_{m} \frac{\partial p(z)}{\partial q_m}\cdot\frac{\partial q_m(z)}{\partial z}$$

Humare case me: $p(z) = L(\theta)$, $z = h_{ij}$ ($i$-th layer ka $j$-th neuron), aur $q_m = a_{i+1,m}$ — kyunki $h_{ij}$ agle layer ke har neuron ko influence karta hai:

$$\frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial h_{ij}} = \sum_{m=1}^{k}\frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial a_{i+1,m}}\cdot\frac{\partial h_{ij}}{\partial a_{i+1,m}} = \sum_{m=1}^{k}\frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial a_{i+1,m}}\, W_{i+1,m,j}$$

(kyunki $a_{i+1} = W_{i+1}h_i + b_{i+1}$, isliye $\frac{\partial a_{i+1,m}}{\partial h_{ij}} = W_{i+1,m,j}$). Ab dekho — ye sum actually ek dot product hai: $(i+1)$-th layer ke gradient vector aur $W_{i+1}$ ke $j$-th column ka. Saare $j$ ek saath likho to:

✦ Hidden Layer Gradients — Backprop ka Core Loop $$\nabla_{h_i} L(\theta) = \left(W_{i+1}\right)^T \nabla_{a_{i+1}} L(\theta) \qquad\qquad \nabla_{a_i} L(\theta) = \nabla_{h_i} L(\theta) \odot [\ldots, g'(a_{ik}), \ldots]$$

Padhne ka tareeka: "layer $i$ ke activation ka gradient = agli layer ki weight matrix ka transpose, agle layer ke pre-activation gradient se multiply." Phir element-wise: activation se pre-activation jaane ke liye activation function ka local derivative $g'(a_i)$ multiply hota hai ($\odot$ = element-wise product). W3 PA Q3 isi ka application tha — influence paths = 10 × 4 = 40!

3.6Gradient w.r.t. Weights aur Biases — Step 3

Ab parameters. Layer $k$ me: $a_k = b_k + W_k h_{k-1}$, isliye $\frac{\partial a_{ki}}{\partial W_{kij}} = h_{k-1,j}$ (kyunki $a_{ki} = \sum_j W_{kij}h_{k-1,j} + b_{ki}$). To:

$$\frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial W_{kij}} = \frac{\partial L(\theta)}{\partial a_{ki}}\cdot h_{k-1,j}$$

Poore matrix ke liye ek sundar compact form hai — 3×3 example se dekho: har entry $(i,j)$ me $\frac{\partial L}{\partial a_{ki}} \cdot h_{k-1,j}$ pada hai, jo exactly ek outer product hai:

✦ Weight aur Bias Gradients $$\nabla_{W_k} L(\theta) = \nabla_{a_k} L(\theta)\cdot h_{k-1}^T \qquad\qquad \nabla_{b_k} L(\theta) = \nabla_{a_k} L(\theta)$$

Weight gradient = (layer ka pre-activation gradient) × (pichli layer ke activations ka transpose). Bias gradient to bilkul simple — bas pre-activation gradient hi hai (kyunki $\frac{\partial a_{ki}}{\partial b_{ki}} = 1$).

◈ Samajh — Outer Product ka Matlab

$\nabla_{W_k} = \nabla_{a_k} h_{k-1}^T$ ka intuitive matlab: kaunse weight kitna badega, ye dono cheezon pe depend karta hai —
(1) us neuron ka error signal ($\nabla_{a_k}$) kitna bada hai
(2) input activation ($h_{k-1}$) kitna active tha.
Jo input zyada "on" tha, uski responsibility zyada — gradient utna hi bada. Deep!

3.7Full Algorithm — Forward + Backward Pseudocode

Ab saare puzzle pieces mil gaye. Poori picture:

  1. Forward propagation se saari $a_i$, $h_i$ aur $\hat{y}$ compute karo
  2. Output layer ka gradient: $\nabla_{a_L} = -(e^{(y)} - \hat{y})$
  3. Har layer $k = L$ se $1$ tak (backwards): weight/bias gradients nikaalo, phir layer neeche ka gradient banao
forward_propagation(θ)Pseudocode
Algorithm: forward_propagation(θ)

for k = 1 to L−1 do
    a_k ← b_k + W_k · h_{k−1}
    h_k ← g(a_k)

a_L ← b_L + W_L · h_{L−1}
ŷ   ← O(a_L)
back_propagation(h₁…h_{L−1}, a₁…a_L, y, ŷ)Pseudocode
Algorithm: back_propagation(...)

// Output layer gradient (softmax + cross-entropy)
∇a_L ← −(e^(y) − ŷ)          // = ŷ − one-hot(y)

for k = L down to 1 do
    // Parameter gradients
    ∇W_k ← ∇a_k · h_{k−1}ᵀ
    ∇b_k ← ∇a_k

    // Layer neeche ke gradients
    ∇h_{k−1} ← (W_k)ᵀ · ∇a_k
    ∇a_{k−1} ← ∇h_{k−1} ⊙ [..., g′(a_{k−1,j}), ...]   // element-wise

// Final step (jo Week 2 se pata hai):
θ ← θ − η · ∇θ          // gradient descent update
⚠ Dhyan — Activation Store Karna Mandatory Nahi

W3 PA ka last question isi pe tha: forward pass me $a_1, h_1, a_2, h_2, \ldots$ store karna helpful hai (standard practice) par mandatory nahi — backward pass me unhe recompute bhi kar sakte ho (zyada compute, kam memory). Ye memory-vs-compute tradeoff modern deep learning frameworks me checkpointing ke naam se use hota hai.

3.8Activation Functions ke Derivatives — $g'$ Nikalna

Backprop me ek hi cheez bachti hai: $g'(a_i)$. Do classic activations ke derivatives poore derive karte hain — exam favorite!

Logistic (Sigmoid): $g(z) = \sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1+e^{-z}}$

Quotient rule se (ya Week 2 wali derivation dobara dekho):

$$g'(z) = \frac{e^{-z}}{(1+e^{-z})^2} = \frac{1}{1+e^{-z}}\cdot\frac{e^{-z}}{1+e^{-z}} = g(z)\left(1 - g(z)\right)$$

Beauty: derivative ko $g(z)$ ke terms me hi likh sakte ho — backward pass me jo $g$ already compute hua hai, wahi se $g'$ free me mil jata hai!

Tanh: $g(z) = \tanh(z) = \frac{e^z + e^{-z}}{e^z - e^{-z}}$

Quotient rule lagao ($u = e^z + e^{-z}$, $v = e^z - e^{-z}$, $u' = e^z - e^{-z} = v$, $v' = e^z + e^{-z} = u$):

$$g'(z) = \frac{v\cdot v - u\cdot u}{v^2} = \frac{v^2 - u^2}{v^2} = 1 - \left(\frac{u}{v}\right)^2 = 1 - \left(g(z)\right)^2$$
✦ Yaad Rakho — Dono Derivatives $$\sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)(1 - \sigma(z)) \qquad\qquad \tanh'(z) = 1 - \tanh^2(z)$$

Dono ko function ki apni value me express kiya ja sakta hai — efficiency ka bonus. $\sigma'(z)$ ki max value $0.25$ ($z=0$ pe), jabki $\tanh'(0) = 1$ — isliye tanh ka gradient signal zyada strong hota hai.

✎ Exam Tip — Backprop Numericals ka Recipe

Quiz 1 (Q12–13) ne exactly ye pattern test kiya. Recipe:
(1) Forward pass karo — har layer ki values likho ($\sigma(1) = 0.7311$ etc.)
(2) Output gradient: sigmoid+CE me $\partial L/\partial z = \hat{y} - y$
(3) Chain rule se peeche jao — har sigmoid ko local slope $\sigma(1-\sigma)$ multiply karo
(4) Round karke answer.
Example: $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w_1} = (\hat{y}-y)\cdot v_1\cdot h_1(1-h_1)\cdot x = (-0.1192)(1)(0.19661)(1) = -0.02$.

✦ Week 3 — Master Summary

(1) $a_i = b_i + W_ih_{i-1}$, $h_i = g(a_i)$; output $\hat{y} = O(a_L)$.
(2) Regression → Linear + MSE; Classification → Softmax + CE ($L = -\log\hat{y}_\ell$ = negative log-likelihood).
(3) $\nabla_{a_L} = \hat{y} - e^{(\ell)}$ (softmax+CE ka magic shortcut).
(4) $\nabla_{h_i} = W_{i+1}^T\nabla_{a_{i+1}}$; $\nabla_{a_i} = \nabla_{h_i}\odot g'(a_i)$ (multi-path chain rule).
(5) $\nabla_{W_k} = \nabla_{a_k}h_{k-1}^T$; $\nabla_{b_k} = \nabla_{a_k}$.
(6) $\sigma' = \sigma(1-\sigma)$, $\tanh' = 1-\tanh^2$.
(7) Activation caching helpful, not mandatory.
Bhai backprop ka poora khel point 3–5 me hai — inhe ratt lo, baaki sab automatic aayega.

Part 03 · Practice Assignment

Week 3 — Practice Assignment (Solved)

8 questions — official key + Hinglish solutions. Shared network: 6 inputs → 12 hidden → 10 hidden → 4 outputs.

Bhai is poore assignment me kuch alag nahi hai — ek hi shared network hai aur uske upar dimensions ginna hai, shapes check karni hai, aur backprop ke teen steps lagane hain. Jo concepts me padha, wahi apply karna hai, bas.

8 QuestionsOfficial key verifiedTopics: Dimensions · Paths · Softmax · Params
❝ Shared Network — Saare Questions Isi Pe Hain

Network: input $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^6$ → hidden layer 1 (12 neurons) → hidden layer 2 (10 neurons) → output layer (4 neurons). Har layer fully connected, har neuron ka bias hai. $W_1$ (input→h1), $W_2$ (h1→h2), $W_3$ (h2→output). Forward equations: $\mathbf{a}_1 = W_1\mathbf{h}_0 + \mathbf{b}_1$ (jahan $\mathbf{h}_0 = \mathbf{x}$), $\mathbf{h}_1 = f(\mathbf{a}_1)$, $\mathbf{a}_2 = W_2\mathbf{h}_1 + \mathbf{b}_2$, $\mathbf{h}_2 = f(\mathbf{a}_2)$, $\mathbf{a}_3 = W_3\mathbf{h}_2 + \mathbf{b}_3$.

Q1Multiple SelectDimensions

$W_1$ aur $a_1$ ke correct dimensions kaunse hain?

  • ✓a. $a_1 \in R^{12 \times 1}$
  • b. $a_1 \in R^{1 \times 12}$
  • c. $a_1 \in R^{1 \times 1}$
  • ✓d. $W_1 \in R^{12 \times 6}$
  • e. $W_1 \in R^{6 \times 12}$
  • f. $W_1 \in R^{12 \times 1}$
Solution kholo
  1. $\mathbf{a}_1 = W_1\mathbf{h}_0 + \mathbf{b}_1$ jahan $\mathbf{h}_0 = \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{6\times 1}$ aur $\mathbf{a}_1$ me 12 hidden-1 pre-activations stacked hain.
  2. Dimension check: $12\times1 = (12\times6)\cdot(6\times1) + 12\times1$ ✓
  3. To $W_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{12\times 6}$ (rows = layer ke neurons, columns = inputs) aur $a_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{12\times 1}$ (column vector).

Answer: a aur d — rule: $W$ ki shape = (fan-out) × (fan-in)

Q2MCQRow Dot Product

$a1_{10}$ (first hidden layer ka 10th neuron) ka output kya hoga? (Bias zero maano)

  • a. $W_1[:,10] \cdot x$
  • b. $W_1 \cdot x$
  • ✓c. $W_1[10,:] \cdot x$
  • d. $W_1[10,:]^T \cdot x$
Solution kholo
  1. Bias zero: $a_{1,10} = $ (10th row of $W_1$) · (input vector).
  2. $W_1[10,:] \in \mathbb{R}^{1\times 6}$ hai aur $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{6\times 1}$ — dot product se scalar milta hai ✓
  3. Baaki options: (a) 10th column (galat object), (b) saare 12 outputs ek saath (scalar nahi), (d) $6\times1$ column (shape mismatch).

Answer: c — single neuron ka pre-activation = uski weight row ka input ke saath dot product

Q3MCQPath Counting

First hidden layer ke 6th neuron ka output final loss tak kitne paths se influence karta hai?

  • a. 2
  • b. 14
  • c. 4
  • ✓d. 40
  • e. 10
  • f. Loss function bina bataye possible nahi
Solution kholo
  1. Ye W3 concept ka direct application hai: $\frac{\partial L}{\partial h_{ij}} = \sum_m \frac{\partial L}{\partial a_{i+1,m}}W_{i+1,m,j}$ — har downstream path se contribution.
  2. Hidden-1 ka neuron → hidden-2 ke saare 10 neurons tak jaata hai (10 edges).
  3. Har hidden-2 neuron → output ke saare 4 neurons tak (har ek se 4 paths).
  4. Total paths $= 10 \times 4 = 40$.

Answer: d — 40 (Bhai bas paths gino — jo humne concepts me dekha tha wahi counting ka khel hai.)

Q4MCQLoss for Classification

Classification problem ke liye kaunse loss functions use kar sakte hain?

  • a. Mean Squared Error only
  • b. Cross Entropy only
  • ✓c. Dono — Mean Squared Error aur Cross Entropy
Solution kholo
  1. Cross-entropy = standard multi-class choice (softmax outputs + one-hot labels ke saath natural fit).
  2. MSE bhi technically use ho sakta hai — classes ko one-hot encode karke squared error nikaal lo. Par ye ideal nahi (non-convex ho jata hai, training slow).
  3. Isliye dono usable hain — CE recommended, MSE possible.

Answer: c

Q5Short AnswerParameter Count

Network me kitne learnable parameters (bias sahit) hain?

Solution kholo
  1. $W_1$: $12 \times 6 = 72$ weights
    $b_1$: $12$ biases
  2. $W_2$: $10 \times 12 = 120$ weights
    $b_2$: $10$ biases
  3. $W_3$: $4 \times 10 = 40$ weights
    $b_3$: $4$ biases
  4. Total $= 72 + 12 + 120 + 10 + 40 + 4 = 258$

Answer: 258 — formula: har layer ke liye $(n_{l-1} + 1) \times n_l$ parameters — bhai ye ek formula saare parameter-count questions ka baap hai, ratt lo

Q6True/FalseSoftmax Bounds

"Softmax output layer me $O$ ka har element 0 se 1 ke beech bounded hota hai." — True ya False?

  • ✓a. True
  • b. False
Solution kholo
  1. $O_j = \frac{e^{a_j}}{\sum_k e^{a_k}}$ — numerator aur denominator dono positive → $O_j \gt 0$.
  2. Sum $= 1$ aur saare elements non-negative → koi bhi element $1$ se bada nahi ho sakta.
  3. To har element $(0, 1)$ me hai — statement true.

Answer: True

Q7MCQZero Input Test

Parameters randomly initialized hain, output layer me linear neuron hai. Agar $x$ ke saare elements zero hon, to final output bhi zero hoga — ye statement:

  • a. Always True
  • ✓b. True only if all the parameters are zero
  • c. Always False
Solution kholo
  1. Output layer: $\mathbf{y} = W_3\mathbf{h}_2 + \mathbf{b}_3$ (linear neuron).
  2. $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ rakho: $\mathbf{a}_1 = W_1\mathbf{0} + \mathbf{b}_1 = \mathbf{b}_1$ — jo zero nahi hai (random init)! To $\mathbf{h}_1 = f(\mathbf{b}_1) \ne \mathbf{0}$, aur aage bhi non-zero hi chalega.
  3. Output exactly tabhi 0 hoga jab saare parameters — weights aur biases — zero hon. Biases hi wo cheez hain jo "zero in ⇒ zero out" tod deti hain.

Answer: b

Q8MCQActivation Caching

Ek student kehta hai: backprop ke liye forward propagation me $a_1, h_1, a_2, h_2, a_3, h_3$ store karna mandatory hai. Student ka argument:

  • a. Right — wo outputs backprop me use hote hain
  • ✓b. Wrong — helpful hai par mandatory nahi
Solution kholo
  1. Stored activations backprop ko $O(1)$ per-layer reuse dete hain — isliye standard practice hai aur memory kharch karti hai.
  2. Par technically backward pass me unhe dobara compute kiya ja sakta hai (extra compute, kam memory) — ya checkpointing (beech-beech me save, beech ke recompute).
  3. Choice application ke constraints pe depend karti hai — mandatory nahi.

Answer: b — memory–compute tradeoff

✎ W3 PA se kya seekhna hai

$W$ ki shape = (fan-out)×(fan-in); neuron = weight row · input; influence paths = downstream fan-outs ka product; params = $\sum_l (n_{l-1}+1)n_l$; softmax → $[0,1]$ + sum 1; biases "zero-in zero-out" todte hain; activation caching optional. Bas — Week 3 ka PA core sorted!

Part 04 · Week 4

Optimizer ka Khandaan

Gradient Descent (GD), Momentum-based GD, Nesterov Accelerated GD, Stochastic & Mini-batch GD, Learning Rate Schedules, Line Search — aur bonus me AdaGrad, RMSProp, AdaDelta, Adam.

≈ 70 min readSource: Lecture 5 notes + standard referencesLevel: Beginner

Dekh bhai, Week 4 me bhi kuch alag hai nahi: wahi purana GD hai, bas usme speed, brake aur naye-naye gadgets laga diye hain. Momentum, Nesterov, AdaGrad, Adam — poora optimizer ka khandaan isi ek idea pe chalta hai. Ek formula samajh liya, sab samajh gaye.

4.1Vanilla GD ki Pareshani

Week 2 ka GD perfect to hai, par ek bug hai: gentle slopes (dheemi dhalwan) pe bahut slow hota hai, kyunki gradient wahan chhota hota hai aur update gradient ke proportional hai. Steep regions me to tez bhaagta hai, par gentle valley me ghutno pe chal padta hai.

Ek aur problem yaad karo: agar gentle slope ko "fix" karne ke liye $\eta$ bada kar do (jaise $\eta = 10$), to steep regions me already bada gradient aur blow up ho jata hai — divergence. Humein chahiye ek learning rate jo gradient ke hisaab se adjust ho sake — is line ne poori modern optimizer research shuru kar di (end me dekhenge!).

4.2Contours — 3D ko 2D Me Padhna

Error surface ka 3D visualization cumbersome hai. Contours lo — surface pe equal-loss lines ka top view (jaise mountains ke map pe contour lines). Reading skill:

  • Contours paas-paas = us direction me steep slope
  • Contours door-door = us direction me gentle slope
✎ Exam Tip — Contour Reading

W4 PA me directly poocha: agar x-direction me contours tightly packed hain aur y-direction me sparse, to kaunsi axis pe slope rapid change hoga? Jawaab: x-axis — kyunki tight contours = bada $|\partial L/\partial x|$. Ek line ka logic: contour density ∝ gradient magnitude.

4.3Momentum-Based Gradient Descent

Intuition: "Agar mujhe baar-baar same direction me jaane ko kaha ja raha hai, to mujhe confidence hona chahiye — aur bade steps lene chahiye." Bilkul waise hi jaise ball slope se ladhakhti hui neeche aati hai — momentum jama kar leti hai. Update rule:

✦ Momentum GD Update Rule $$u_t = \beta u_{t-1} + \nabla w_t \qquad\qquad w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta\, u_t$$

jahan $u_{-1} = 0$, $u_0 = \nabla w_0$, aur $0 \le \beta \lt 1$. $u_t$ = exponentially weighted average of current and all past gradients — unroll karke dekho: $u_t = \sum_{\tau=0}^{t}\beta^{t-\tau}\nabla w_\tau$. Purane gradients ka contribution $\beta$ ki power se decay hota hai (geometric decay).

Unrolling dikhata hai: $u_0 = \nabla w_0$, $u_1 = \beta\nabla w_0 + \nabla w_1$, $u_2 = \beta^2\nabla w_0 + \beta\nabla w_1 + \nabla w_2$… Matlab gradient ke history ko bhi yaad rakhta hai — consistent direction me accumulate karke bade effective steps banta hai.

Dekh bhai, momentum me bhi kuch hai nahi — bas GD ko ek yaadasht de di: purani direction yaad rakho aur naye gradient se mix karte jao. Ek formula aur khel khatam.

momentum_gd.pyPython
def do_mgd(max_epochs):
    w, b, eta = -2, -2, 1.0
    prev_uw, prev_ub, beta = 0, 0, 0.9

    for i in range(max_epochs):
        dw, db = 0, 0
        for x, y in zip(X, Y):
            dw += grad_w(w, b, x, y)
            db += grad_b(w, b, x, y)

        uw = beta*prev_uw + eta*dw     # history + current
        ub = beta*prev_ub + eta*db
        w = w - uw
        b = b - ub
        prev_uw, prev_ub = uw, ub

Momentum ka behaviour — fast par overshoot bhi

Gentle regions me momentum GD bade steps leta hai — kyunki accumulated velocity saath le jaati hai. Par ek side-effect hai: moving fast hamesha achha nahi. Agar error surface me ek narrow minima-valley hai (dono taraf high error), to momentum valley ke andar ghus kar ek taraf se dusri taraf oscillate karta hai — u-turns maarta rehta hai, kyunki velocity use wapas valley se bahar pheink deti hai. Phir bhi, in u-turns ke baad bhi ye vanilla GD se faster converge karta hai: course ke demo me 50 iterations me momentum error 0.00001 tak pahunch gaya, jabki vanilla GD 0.16 pe hi atka tha!

4.4Nesterov Accelerated Gradient (NAG) — Look Before You Leap

Oscillations kam kaise karein? NAG ka idea: "kudne se pehle dekho". Momentum me hum jaante hain ki hum kam se kam $\beta u_{t-1}$ move karne wale hain (velocity), phir thoda aur $\nabla w_t$ ke hisaab se. To gradient ko us anticipated (lookahead) position pe compute kyun na karein?

✦ NAG Update Rule $$u_t = \beta u_{t-1} + \nabla\left(w_t - \beta u_{t-1}\right) \qquad\qquad w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta\, u_t$$

Farak sirf itna hai: gradient ab current $w_t$ pe nahi, balki lookahead point $w_t - \beta u_{t-1}$ pe evaluate hota hai. Isse NAG apna course pehle hi correct kar leta hai — valley ke bahar jaane se pehle hi brake lag jata hai.

nag.py — dekho lookahead kahan haiPython
def do_nag(max_epochs):
    w, b, eta = -2, -2, 1.0
    prev_vw, prev_vb, beta = 0, 0, 0.9

    for i in range(max_epochs):
        dw, db = 0, 0
        # PARTIAL update — lookahead point
        v_w = beta*prev_vw
        v_b = beta*prev_vb
        for x, y in zip(X, Y):
            # gradient AT the look-ahead position
            dw += grad_w(w - v_w, b - v_b, x, y)
            db += grad_b(w - v_w, b - v_b, x, y)

        vw = beta*prev_vw + eta*dw
        vb = beta*prev_vb + eta*db
        w = w - vw
        b = b - vb
        prev_vw, prev_vb = vw, vb
✦ Momentum vs NAG — Ek Line Me

Lookahead ki wajah se NAG course quicker correct karta hai → oscillations smaller → valley se bahar jaane ke chances fewer. Stochastic versions me bhi ye relative advantage bana rehta hai (NAG chhote u-turns leta hai), aur dono plain SGD se tez hain. Demo numbers: SGD-Momentum β=0.5, SGD-NAG β=0.85 — 500 steps ke baad plain SGD (black) abhi high error pe tha, Momentum aur NAG convergence ke paas.

4.5Stochastic & Mini-Batch Gradient Descent

Ab ek digression — "stochastic" (random-ish) versions. Vanilla GD me notice karo: algorithm poora data dekh kar hi ek update karta hai. Kyun? Kyunki wo gradient true gradient hai — har point ke gradient ka sum. Koi approximation nahi, isliye theoretical guarantee bhi hai (chhote $\eta$ pe har step loss ghatata hai). Par flipside: 10 lakh points ka dataset hai? Ek update ke liye 10 lakh gradient calculations — bahut slow!

Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) — 1 point, 1 update

SGD har single data point ke baad update kar deta hai: 1 epoch = $N$ updates. Gradient ab "stochastic estimate" hai — jaise ek baar coin toss karke $P(\text{heads})$ estimate karna. Guarantee khatam: har step pe loss ghat-ega, aisa zaroori nahi!

Oscillations kyun aate hain?

SGD me dher saare oscillations dikhte hain. Reason: har point greedy decision leta hai — apne liye best direction me parameters dhakelta hai, bina ye jaane ki dusre points pe kya asar padega. Ek point ke liye favorable update dusre ko nuksan de sakta hai — almost as if data points are competing with each other!

Mini-Batch GD — beech ka rasta

Behtar gradient estimate ke liye $k$ points ka batch lo — update har $k$ points ke baad. Ab estimate thoda better hai (analogy: coin ko 25 baar toss karke $P(\text{heads})$ estimate karna). $k$ jitna bada, estimates utne accurate — par oscillations kabhi khatam nahi hote jab tak approximate gradient use ho raha hai (true gradient ke saamne).

Algorithm# Updates in 1 epochNote
Vanilla (Batch) GD1True gradient, guaranteed decrease (chhote η pe), par slow per update
Stochastic GD$N$1 update per point — noisy, par cheap updates
Mini-Batch GD$N/B$$B$ = mini-batch size — sweet spot (practically sabse zyada used)

1 epoch = one pass over entire data1 step = 1 parameter updateN = # data points, B = batch size

minibatch_sgd.py — batch size k=25Python
def do_minibatch_sgd():
    w, b, eta, max_epochs = -2, -2, 1.0, 500
    mini_batch_size = 25

    for i in range(max_epochs):
        dw, db, num_points_seen = 0, 0, 0
        for x, y in zip(X, Y):
            dw += grad_w(x, w, b, y)
            db += grad_b(x, w, b, y)
            num_points_seen += 1

            if num_points_seen % mini_batch_size == 0:
                w = w - eta*dw     # har k points ke baad update
                b = b - eta*db
                dw, db = 0, 0

Momentum aur NAG ke bhi stochastic versions bante hain — same idea, gradient ab mini-batch se aata hai. Mini-batch versions of momentum/NAG bhi possible hain (exercise!).

✎ Exam Tip — Updates Counting (Direct Questions!)

Ye table se do official quiz questions ban-chuke hain:
(1) Vanilla GD pe "kitne updates per epoch?" → 1 (chahe 100,000 points hon)
(2) Mini-batch $B=50$, $N = 100{,}000$ → $100000/50 = \mathbf{2000}$ updates/epoch
(3) W4 PA: SGD me 10,000 samples × 10 epochs = 100,000 updates
(4) Line search GD me — sirf 1 update per epoch (best η select hota hai, trials updates nahi hote!).
Formula yaad rakho: $\lceil N/B \rceil$.

4.6Learning Rate aur Momentum ke Tips

Initial learning rate kaise choose karein?

  • Log-scale search: $\eta \in \{0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0\}$ try karo — kuch epochs chalao, best pick karo.
  • Fine search: best value ke aas-paas try karo (jaise 0.1 best nikla → ab 0.05, 0.2, 0.3 dekho).
  • Disclaimer (slides ka verbatim): "these are just heuristics… no clear winner strategy".

Learning rate annealing — dheere-dheere kam karna

Shuru me bade steps (tez progress), end me chhote (fine convergence). Teen classic schedules:

ScheduleFormulaIdea
Step Decayhar 5 epochs me $\eta$ ko half karo; ya jab validation error pichle epoch se badh jayeManual but popular
Exponential Decay$\eta = \eta_0\, e^{-kt}$Smooth exponential girawat; $\eta_0, k$ hyperparameters, $t$ = step number
1/t Decay$\eta = \dfrac{\eta_0}{1 + kt}$Polynomial-style decay — exponential se dheemi

Momentum ka schedule (Sutskever et al. 2013)

$$\beta_t = \min\left(1 - 2^{-1-\log_2(\lfloor t/250 \rfloor + 1)},\ \beta_{max}\right), \quad \beta_{max} \in \{0.999, 0.995, 0.99, 0.9, 0\}$$

Idea: shuru me momentum kam, dheere-dheere badhao — taaki shuruaati large noisy steps momentum se amplify na ho jayein.

4.7Line Search — Har Step Pe Best η

Ek aur trick: har step pe gradient nikalne ke baad kai candidate $\eta$ values try karo (jaise $[0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10]$), har candidate ke liye temporary update karke loss dekho, aur jis $\eta$ se loss sabse kam aaya, wahi update accept karo. Essentially har step pe available choices me se best $\eta$ use kar rahe ho.

line_search_gd.pyPython
def do_line_search_gd(max_epochs):
    w, b, etas = -2, -2, [0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10]

    for i in range(max_epochs):
        dw, db = 0, 0
        for x, y in zip(X, Y):
            dw += grad_w(w, b, x, y)
            db += grad_b(w, b, x, y)

        min_error = 10000   # some large value
        for eta in etas:
            temp_w = w - eta*dw
            temp_b = b - eta*db
            if error(temp_w, temp_b) < min_error:
                best_w = temp_w
                best_b = temp_b
                min_error = error(best_w, best_b)
        w, b = best_w, best_b   # best-η update accepted

Flipside: har step me bahut zyada computations — har $\eta$ ke liye loss evaluate karna padta hai. Convergence vanilla se faster hoti hai; oscillations dikhte hain par wo momentum/NAG wale se alag type ke hain (ye ek hi ray par alternating step-sizes se bante hain, overshoot se nahi).

4.8Bonus — Adaptive Optimizers: AdaGrad se Adam tak

Slides me teaser diya gaya tha: "It would be good to have a learning rate which could adjust to the gradient… we will see a few such algorithms soon." Week 4 ki deck wahan khatam ho gayi, par ye concepts itne important hain ki bina inke Week 4 adhoora hai. To ye raha bonus section — standard formulations ke saath (Kingma & Ba 2015, Duchi et al. 2011, Tieleman & Hinton 2012, Zeiler 2012).

Core Idea: Per-Parameter Learning Rate

Vanilla GD sab parameters ke liye same $\eta$ use karta hai. Par real networks me kuch parameters ke gradients hamesha sparse/chhote hote hain (rare features), kuch ke bade. Adaptive optimizers har parameter ki gradient history dekh kar uska apna effective learning rate banate hain.

OptimizerUpdate RuleKey IdeaKamzori
AdaGrad $s_t = s_{t-1} + (\nabla w_t)^2$
$w_{t+1} = w_t - \dfrac{\eta}{\sqrt{s_t + \epsilon}}\,\nabla w_t$		 Har parameter ki gradient ka accumulated squared sum — jis parameter ka history bada, uska effective η chhota $s_t$ sirf badhta rehta hai → learning rate eventually zero ho jaati hai (training ruk sakti hai)
RMSProp $s_t = \beta s_{t-1} + (1-\beta)(\nabla w_t)^2$
$w_{t+1} = w_t - \dfrac{\eta}{\sqrt{s_t + \epsilon}}\,\nabla w_t$		 AdaGrad + exponential decay — purana history bhool jata hai (moving average of squared gradients) — (practically solid; Hinton ka Coursera favourite)
AdaDelta $s_t = \rho s_{t-1} + (1-\rho)(\nabla w_t)^2$
$\Delta w_t = -\dfrac{\sqrt{r_{t-1}+\epsilon}}{\sqrt{s_t+\epsilon}}\nabla w_t$		 RMSProp jaisa + learning rate ki zaroorat hi khatam (Δw ke RMS se unit banta hai) Extra state ($r_t$) maintain karna
Adam $u_t = \beta_1 u_{t-1} + (1-\beta_1)\nabla w_t$
$s_t = \beta_2 s_{t-1} + (1-\beta_2)(\nabla w_t)^2$
$\hat{u}_t = \frac{u_t}{1-\beta_1^t},\ \hat{s}_t = \frac{s_t}{1-\beta_2^t}$
$w_{t+1} = w_t - \dfrac{\eta}{\sqrt{\hat{s}_t}+\epsilon}\hat{u}_t$		 Momentum (1st moment) + RMSProp (2nd moment) + bias correction — dono duniyaon ka best Thoda zyada memory (2 moving averages)
✦ Adam — Default Optimizer Kyun Hai

Adam = Adaptive Moment estimation. Wo momentum ki tarah gradient ka exponentially weighted average rakhta hai ($u_t$ — direction), aur RMSProp ki tarah squared gradients ka ($s_t$ — scale). Bias correction ($1-\beta^t$ divide karna) shuruaati steps me zeros-biased estimates ko theek karta hai. Typical values: $\beta_1 = 0.9$, $\beta_2 = 0.999$, $\eta = 0.001$, $\epsilon = 10^{-8}$. NLP/CV me default choice isi liye hai. (Note: paper-1503 wale quiz me "Adam paper" ka zikr reference ke taur pe tha — Adam = Kingma & Ba, 2014/2015.)

◈ Samajh — Family Tree

Ek line me poora khandaan: GD ne dikhaya rasta → Momentum ne speed di (history yaad) → NAG ne akal di (lookahead) → SGD/Mini-batch ne practical banaya (cheap updates) → AdaGrad ne per-parameter learning rate diya → RMSProp ne usse "kabhi na rukne wala" banaya (decay) → Adam ne sab merge kar diya. Interview me "Adam kya hai?" ka best answer: "Momentum + RMSProp with bias correction."

✦ Week 4 — Master Summary

(1) GD gentle slopes pe slow; bada η → steep me blow-up.
(2) Contours: tight = steep.
(3) Momentum: $u_t = \beta u_{t-1} + \nabla w_t$ — exponentially weighted history; tez par valley me u-turns.
(4) NAG: gradient at lookahead $w_t - \beta u_{t-1}$ — chhote oscillations.
(5) Updates/epoch: GD=1, SGD=$N$, Mini-batch=$N/B$.
(6) LR schedules: step, $\eta_0e^{-kt}$, $\eta_0/(1+kt)$.
(7) Line search: har step best-η (par costly).
(8) Adaptive: AdaGrad→RMSProp→AdaDelta→Adam (momentum + RMS + bias correction).
Bhai optimizer ka khandaan bas itna hi hai — har naya optimizer purane wale me ek fix hai. Ek line samajh li, sab samajh liye.

7 QuestionsOfficial key verifiedTopics: GD · Momentum · NAG · SGD
Q1MCQSlopes at x=1

$f_1(x) = \log_2(x)$, $f_2(x) = \log_e(x)$, $f_3(x) = \log_{10}(x)$, $f_4(x) = 0.5x^2$ — inme se kis function ka slope $x = 1$ pe sabse steep hai?

  • ✓a. $f_1(x) = \log_2(x)$
  • b. $f_2(x) = \log_e(x)$
  • c. $f_3(x) = \log_{10}(x)$
  • d. $f_4(x) = 0.5x^2$
Solution kholo
  1. $f_1'(x) = \frac{1}{x\ln 2}$ → $f_1'(1) = 1/\ln 2 \approx 1.4427$
  2. $f_2'(x) = \frac{1}{x}$ → $f_2'(1) = 1$
  3. $f_3'(x) = \frac{1}{x\ln 10}$ → $f_3'(1) \approx 0.4343$
  4. $f_4'(x) = x$ → $f_4'(1) = 1$
  5. Compare: $1.4427 \gt 1 = 1 \gt 0.4343$ — winner $\log_2$! (General rule: log ka base chhota → curve steeper.)

Answer: a — log₂(x) (Bhai bas derivative nikaalo aur compare karo — pure slope ka khel hai.)

Q2True/FalseContour Reading

Contour plot me $x$-direction me contours tightly packed hain, $y$-direction me sparse. Ek aadmi $-1$ se $+1$ tak $x$-axis aur $y$-axis dono pe chalta hai. "Slope $x$-axis pe $y$-axis se zyada rapidly change hota hai" — True ya False?

  • ✓a. True
  • b. False
  • c. Not possible to say
Solution kholo
  1. Contour density = gradient magnitude ka visual signal.
  2. $x$-direction me lines paas-paas → same distance pe loss zyada change → $|\partial L/\partial x|$ bada.
  3. Isliye slope $x$-axis pe sach me rapid change hota hai. (Isi elongated-contour valley ne to momentum wala problem diya tha!)

Answer: True

Q3Multiple SelectGD Step Size

Update rule: $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta\nabla w_t$. GD ka behaviour select karo:

  • ✓a. Gentle loss surface pe weight update tiny hota hai
  • b. Steep loss surface pe weight update tiny hota hai
  • ✓c. Steep loss surface pe weight update large hota hai
  • d. Gentle loss surface pe weight update large hota hai
Solution kholo
  1. Update magnitude $= \eta\|\nabla w_t\|$ — gradient ke proportional.
  2. Gentle surface → chhota gradient → tiny update (a) ✓
  3. Steep surface → bada gradient → large update (c) ✓

Answer: a aur c

Q4Short AnswerMomentum History

Momentum rules: $u_t = \beta u_{t-1} + \nabla\mathbf{w}_t$, $\mathbf{w}_{t+1} = \mathbf{w}_t - \eta u_t$. Algorithm 100 iterations chala ($t = 0,\ldots,99$), $u_{-1} = 0$, $\beta = 0.9$. $u_{99}$ me $\nabla\mathbf{w}_0$ ka contribution kya hai?

Solution kholo
  1. Unroll karo:
    $u_0 = \nabla w_0$
    $u_1 = \beta\nabla w_0 + \nabla w_1$
    $u_2 = \beta^2\nabla w_0 + \beta\nabla w_1 + \nabla w_2$…
  2. General: $u_{99} = \beta^{99}\nabla w_0 + \beta^{98}\nabla w_1 + \cdots + \nabla w_{99}$
  3. $\nabla w_0$ ka coefficient $= \beta^{99} = 0.9^{99} = 0.0000295\ldots$
  4. 6 decimal places tak (official key truncate karti hai): $0.000029$

Answer: 0.000029 (note: round karne par 0.000030 hota — official key truncation use karti hai; concept = $\beta^t$ geometric decay of history)

Q5True/FalseNAG Lookahead

"NAG hamesha momentum-based GD se aage (ahead) course correction karta hai." — True ya False?

  • ✓a. True
  • b. False
Solution kholo
  1. NAG me gradient current position pe nahi, anticipated future position $w_t - \beta u_{t-1}$ pe compute hota hai.
  2. Isliye correction "ahead of time" milti hai — course-description me yahi standard statement hai (official key: True).
  3. Chhoti si caveat: "always" ka word strong hai, par is course ki official key ke hisaab se True hi hai.

Answer: True

Q6MCQSGD Update Count

10,000 samples ka training dataset hai, aur stochastic gradient descent use ho raha hai. 10 epochs training ke baad weights kitni baar update hue?

  • a. 1000
  • b. 10000
  • ✓c. 100000
  • d. 10
Solution kholo
  1. SGD = update after every sample → 1 epoch me 10,000 updates.
  2. 10 epochs → $10{,}000 \times 10 = 100{,}000$ updates.

Answer: c — 100000

Q7MCQLine Search Updates

Same 10,000 samples, par ab GD + line search ($\eta \in [0.01, 0.1, 1, 2, 10]$) use hua. 10 epochs me weights kitni baar update hue? (Note: har update ke liye current loss aur previous loss ka absolute difference high hona chahiye)

  • a. 50
  • b. 500000
  • c. 100000
  • ✓d. 10
Solution kholo
  1. Full-batch GD = 1 gradient per epoch → sirf 1 weight update per epoch.
  2. Line search sirf $\eta$ select karti hai — 5 candidate η try karna = 5 evaluations, 5 updates nahi!
  3. Sirf best-η wala update apply hota hai (jisse loss sabse zyada girta hai) → 10 epochs = 10 updates.

Answer: d — 10 (is question me official PDF me tick print nahi hua tha — printed explanation se verified: "In one epoch, one update with the best learning rate.")

✎ W4 PA se kya seekhna hai

Log base chhota = steep; contour density = gradient magnitude; GD step ∝ local gradient; momentum history me $\beta^t$ decay; NAG = lookahead correction; SGD me $N$ updates/epoch; line search me evaluations ≠ updates. Ye 7 punchlines exam ke liye kaafi hain!

Q2 · 2 marksMCQMP Neuron

MP neuron ke liye kaunsa statement true hai?

  • a. Non-linear decision boundary wale boolean functions implement kar sakta hai
  • ✓b. Linearly separable boolean functions linear decision boundary ke saath implement kar sakta hai
  • c. Real-valued functions approximate kar sakta hai
  • d. Weights/threshold adjust karke XOR ko accurately represent kar sakta hai
Solution kholo
  1. MP neuron fires iff $\sum_i x_i \ge \theta$ — ye input space me ek half-space hai, yaani linear boundary.
  2. To sirf linearly separable functions (AND, OR, NAND, NOR…) ban sakte hain.
  3. XOR non-separable hai → (d) ✗
    Real-valued approximation ka concept hi nahi → (c) ✗.

Answer: b (bhai bas linear separability wali line yaad rakho — MP ka poora khel isi pe khada hai)

Q3 · 4 marksMCQReLU Homogeneity

Shallow network: scalar input $x$, hidden layer 3 neurons: $h_{11} = a(b_{11}+w_{11}x)$, $h_{12} = a(b_{12}+w_{12}x)$, $h_{13} = a(b_{13}+w_{13}x)$; output $y = b_{21} + w_{21}h_{11} + w_{22}h_{12} + w_{23}h_{13}$. Ab $b_{11}, w_{11}$ ko constant $\alpha \ne 0$ se multiply kiya aur $w_{21}$ ko same $\alpha$ se divide kiya. Kaunsa statement correct hai?

  • ✓a. Output unchanged rehta hai agar activation ReLU ho aur $\alpha \gt 0$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$
  • b. Output unchanged rehta hai agar activation ReLU ho aur $\alpha \lt 0$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$
  • c. Output unchanged rehta hai agar activation sigmoid ho aur $\alpha \gt 0$
  • d. Transformation ke baad contribution $w_{21}h_{11}$ sab $x$ aur sab $\alpha \ne 0$ ke liye unchanged rehta hai
Solution kholo
  1. Transform ke baad: $h_{11}' = a(\alpha(b_{11}+w_{11}x))$ aur output contribution $\frac{w_{21}}{\alpha}h_{11}'$.
  2. ReLU positively homogeneous hai: $\alpha \gt 0$ ke liye $\text{ReLU}(\alpha z) = \alpha\,\text{ReLU}(z)$ → $h_{11}' = \alpha h_{11}$ → $\frac{w_{21}}{\alpha}\cdot\alpha h_{11} = w_{21}h_{11}$ — output same! (a) ✓
  3. $\alpha \lt 0$: $\text{ReLU}(\alpha z) = -\alpha\,\text{ReLU}(-z) \ne \alpha\,\text{ReLU}(z)$ (jaise $z \gt 0$: LHS $=0$) → (b) ✗
  4. Sigmoid homogeneous nahi: $\sigma(\alpha z) \ne \alpha\sigma(z)$ → (c) ✗
    aur (d) "for ALL α" already dono counterexamples se fail.

Answer: a — concept: positive homogeneity of ReLU

Q4 · 3 marksMultiple SelectXOR Construction

MLP: 2 binary inputs, 2 hidden neurons, 1 output. $h_1 = \text{step}(-0.5 + x_1 + x_2)$ (OR), $h_2 = \text{step}(-1.5 + x_1 + x_2)$ (AND), $y = \text{step}(w_0 + w_1h_1 + w_2h_2)$. $w_0 = -0.5,\ w_1 = 1$ diya hai. XOR ke liye $w_2$ ke possible choices?

  • a. $0.5$
  • ✓b. $-0.55$
  • ✓c. $-0.60$
  • d. $1$
Solution kholo
  1. Truth table pe $y = \text{step}(-0.5 + h_1 + w_2 h_2)$ check karo:
  2. $(0,0)$: $h=(0,0)$ → $\text{step}(-0.5) = 0$ ✓ (koi bhi $w_2$)
  3. $(0,1),(1,0)$: $h=(1,0)$ → $\text{step}(0.5) = 1$ ✓ (koi bhi $w_2$)
  4. $(1,1)$: $h=(1,1)$ → chahiye $\text{step}(0.5 + w_2) = 0$ ⇒ $0.5 + w_2 \lt 0$ ⇒ $w_2 \lt -0.5$
  5. Options me $-0.55$ aur $-0.60$ hi $-0.5$ se neeche hain.

Answer: b, c

Q5 · 2 marksShort AnswerParameter Count

Regression network: input $x \in \mathbb{R}^{10}$ → 2 hidden layers (har ek me 5 sigmoid neurons) → output layer 1 sigmoid neuron. Total parameters?

Solution kholo
  1. Layer 1 (10→5): $10\times5 + 5 = 55$
  2. Layer 2 (5→5): $5\times5 + 5 = 30$
  3. Output (5→1): $5\times1 + 1 = 6$
  4. Total $= 55 + 30 + 6 = 91$ — formula: har layer $(n_{l-1}+1)\times n_l$

Answer: 91 (Bhai formula ek hi hai — har layer $(n_{l-1}+1)\times n_l$; jodo aur done.)

Q6 · 3 marksShort AnswerExponential Decay

12 samples, vanilla GD, 4 epochs. Learning rate: $\eta_t = 0.8\,e^{-0.2t}$ (iteration index $t$ zero se shuru, sirf parameter update pe increment). Training ke end me learning rate ki value?

Solution kholo
  1. Vanilla (batch) GD = 1 update per epoch → 4 epochs = 4 updates → iteration indices $t = 0, 1, 2, 3$.
  2. Sequential values: $\eta_0 = 0.8$, $\eta_1 = 0.8e^{-0.2} = 0.655$, $\eta_2 = 0.8e^{-0.4} = 0.536$, $\eta_3 = 0.8e^{-0.6} = 0.439$
  3. Training ke end me last-used LR = $\eta_3 = 0.43905 \approx 0.439$ (official range 0.436–0.442 ✓)

Answer: 0.439 — dhyan: last used value poochi hai, agli (unused) value nahi

Q7 · 4 marksShort AnswerSigmoid + MSE Update

Recommendation model: $\hat{y}_i = \frac{1}{1+e^{-(w^Tx_i+b)}}$, squared-error loss $L(w,b) = \frac{1}{n}\sum(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$. Training example: $\mathbf{x} = [1, 1]^T$, $y = 1$; init $\mathbf{w} = [0,0]^T$, $b = 0$. Ek update ($\eta = 1$) ke baad loss kya hai? (2 decimal)

Solution kholo
  1. Initial: $z_0 = w^Tx + b = 0$ → $\hat{y}_0 = \sigma(0) = 0.5$
    loss $= (1-0.5)^2 = 0.25$
  2. Gradients ($n=1$):
    $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w} = -2(y-\hat{y})\hat{y}(1-\hat{y})x = -2(0.5)(0.25)[1,1]^T = [-0.25,-0.25]^T$
    $\frac{\partial L}{\partial b} = -0.25$
  3. Update ($\eta=1$): $\mathbf{w} = [0.25, 0.25]^T$, $b = 0.25$
  4. Naya prediction: $z_1 = 0.25 + 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.75$ → $\hat{y}_1 = \sigma(0.75) = 0.6792$
  5. Naya loss $= (1 - 0.6792)^2 = 0.1029 \approx 0.10$ (official range 0.08–0.12 ✓)

Answer: 0.10

Q8–Q9 · ComprehensionNAND Perceptron4 marks

Shared data: NAND truth table: $(0,0)\to1$, $(0,1)\to1$, $(1,0)\to1$, $(1,1)\to0$. Perceptron: $f(x) = 1$ iff $\sum_{i=0}^{2}w_ix_i \ge 0$, jahan $x_0 = 1$.

Q8 (1 mark): Kya NAND linearly separable hai?
Q9 (3 marks): Kaunse weights $w_0, w_1, w_2$ NAND produce karenge?
Options (Q9): (a) $w_0{=}2, w_1{=}-1, w_2{=}-1$ · (b) $w_0{=}1, w_1{=}-1, w_2{=}-1$ · (c) $w_0{=}-2, w_1{=}-1, w_2{=}-1$ · (d) $w_0{=}0.5, w_1{=}-0.25, w_2{=}-0.25$

  • ✓Q8: (a) Yes — linearly separable hai
  • ✓Q9: (b) $w_0 = 1,\ w_1 = -1,\ w_2 = -1$
Solution kholo
  1. Q8: Line $x_1 + x_2 = 1.5$ ke ek taraf $(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)$ (output 1) aur dusri taraf $(1,1)$ (output 0) — separated! Answer: Yes.
  2. Q9 (b) verify:
    $(0,0)$: $1 \ge 0 \to 1$ ✓
    $(0,1)$: $0 \ge 0 \to 1$ ✓
    $(1,0)$: $0 \ge 0 \to 1$ ✓
    $(1,1)$: $-1 \lt 0 \to 0$ ✓ — perfect NAND!
  3. Baaki options:
    (a) $(1,1)$ pe $2-1-1 = 0 \ge 0 \to 1$ ✗
    (c) $(0,0)$ pe $-2 \lt 0 \to 0$ ✗
    (d) $(1,1)$ pe $0.5-0.25-0.25 = 0 \ge 0 \to 1$ ✗.

Answer: Q8: a (Yes) · Q9: b

Q10–Q11 · ComprehensionPLA Trace5 marks

Shared data: Dataset: $(2,1,+1)$, $(-1,-2,-1)$, $(1,3,+1)$, $(-2,-1,-1)$ — isi order me. Init $\mathbf{w}_0 = [0,0]^T$. Rule: $y = +1$ if $w^Tx \ge 0$ else $-1$; misclassification pe $w \leftarrow w + yx$ ($\eta = 1$).

Q10 (3 marks): Ek epoch ke baad updated weight vector?
Options: (a) $[3,4]^T$ · (b) $[1,2]^T$ · (c) $[1,3]^T$ · (d) $[-2,-1]^T$
Q11 (2 marks): "Ek epoch ke baad convergence ho gayi" — True ya False?

  • ✓Q10: (b) $\mathbf{w} = [1, 2]^T$
  • ✓Q11: (a) True
Solution kholo
  1. Point 1 $(2,1,+1)$: $w^Tx = 0 \ge 0$ → predicted $+1$ = label ✓ no update. $w = [0,0]$
  2. Point 2 $(-1,-2,-1)$: $w^Tx = 0 \ge 0$ → predicted $+1 \ne -1$ ✗ → update: $w = [0,0] + (-1)[-1,-2] = [1,2]$
  3. Point 3 $(1,3,+1)$: $w^Tx = 1 + 6 = 7 \ge 0$ → $+1$ ✓ no update
  4. Point 4 $(-2,-1,-1)$: $w^Tx = -2 - 2 = -4 \lt 0$ → $-1$ ✓ no update
  5. Ek epoch ke baad: $\mathbf{w} = [1, 2]^T$.
  6. Q11: Is $w$ se charo points:
    $2+2 = 4 \ge 0$ ✓
    $-1-4 = -5 \lt 0$ ✓
    $1+6 = 7 \ge 0$ ✓
    $-2-2 = -4 \lt 0$ ✓ — sab sahi → no more updates → converged. True!

Answer: Q10: b · Q11: True

Q12–Q13 · ComprehensionSigmoid Net + Backprop7 marks

Shared data: Binary classification network: 1 input → hidden layer (2 sigmoid neurons) → 1 sigmoid output. Cross-entropy loss. Values: $w_1 = 1, b_{11} = 0$; $w_2 = -1, b_{12} = 0$; $v_1 = 1, v_2 = 1, b_{21} = 1$; input $x = 1$, true label $y = 1$. Model: $h_1 = \sigma(w_1x + b_{11})$, $h_2 = \sigma(w_2x + b_{12})$, $\hat{y} = \sigma(v_1h_1 + v_2h_2 + b_{21})$.

Q12 (3 marks): Predicted output $\hat{y}$? (2 decimal)
Q13 (4 marks): $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w_1}$? (2 decimal)

Solution kholo
  1. Q12 forward pass:
    $h_1 = \sigma(1) = 0.7311$
    $h_2 = \sigma(-1) = 0.2689$
  2. Output pre-activation: $z = 1(0.7311) + 1(0.2689) + 1 = 2.0$ → $\hat{y} = \sigma(2) = 0.8808 \approx \mathbf{0.88}$ ✓ (range 0.86–0.90)
  3. Q13 backprop: sigmoid + CE → $\frac{\partial L}{\partial z} = \hat{y} - y = 0.8808 - 1 = -0.1192$
  4. Chain rule: $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w_1} = (\hat{y}-y)\cdot v_1\cdot h_1(1-h_1)\cdot x$
  5. $h_1(1-h_1) = 0.7311 \times 0.2689 = 0.19661$ → $(-0.1192)(1)(0.19661)(1) = -0.0234 \approx \mathbf{-0.02}$ ✓ (range −0.04–0.00)

Answer: Q12: 0.88 · Q13: −0.02

Q14–Q15 · ComprehensionMomentum Mini-batch6 marks

Shared data: Linear regression $\hat{y} = wx$, loss $J(w) = \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}(wx_i - y_i)^2$ ($m$ = batch size). Mini-batch size 2, $\eta = 0.1$, $\beta = 0.9$. Init: $w_0 = 1$, $u_{-1} = 0$. Rules: $u_t = \beta u_{t-1} + \nabla J(w_t)$, $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta u_t$. First mini-batch: $(x,y) = (1,2), (2,4)$.

Q14 (3 marks): $\nabla J(w_0)$ is mini-batch ke liye?
Options: (a) $-2.5$ · (b) $-5.0$ · (c) $-7.5$ · (d) $5.0$
Q15 (3 marks): Velocity $u_0$ after first iteration? (1 decimal)

  • ✓Q14: (a) $-2.5$
  • ✓Q15: $-2.5$
Solution kholo
  1. Q14: $\nabla J(w) = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}(wx_i - y_i)x_i$
  2. $w_0 = 1$: $(1\cdot1 - 2)(1) = -1$
    $(1\cdot2 - 4)(2) = -4$
  3. $\nabla J(w_0) = \frac{-1 + (-4)}{2} = -2.5$ ✓
  4. Q15: $u_0 = \beta u_{-1} + \nabla J(w_0) = 0.9\times0 + (-2.5) = -2.5$ ✓

Answer: Q14: a (−2.5) · Q15: −2.5

Formula / ConceptYaad rakhne wali baat (exam-ready)Is paper me
MP neuron rule$y = 1$ iff $\sum_i x_i \ge \theta$ — linear boundary, sirf linearly separable functions; inhibitory input 1 ho → output forced 0Q2
ReLU homogeneity$\text{ReLU}(\alpha z) = \alpha\,\text{ReLU}(z)$ — weights ko constant $\alpha$ se scale karo to network ka output bhi scale ho jata haiQ3
XOR constructionXOR sirf hidden layer se banta hai — 2 step neurons (OR + AND type) + output layer ka combination; single layer kabhi kaafi nahiQ4
Parameter countingweights $= \sum (\text{in} \times \text{out})$ + biases $= \sum \text{neurons}$ — input layer me koi parameter nahi hotaQ5
Exponential LR decay$\eta_t = \eta_0 e^{-kt}$ — shuru me bade steps, end me fine-tuning; $t$ = update index, seedha plug karke value nikaloQ6
Sigmoid + MSE gradient$\frac{\partial L}{\partial w} = -2(y - \hat{y})\,\hat{y}(1-\hat{y})\,x$ — chain: loss → $\hat{y}$ → $z$ → $w$Q7
NAND + separabilityNAND linearly separable hai — bias $x_0 = 1$ ke saath $w_0, w_1, w_2$ choose karke chaaro truth-table rows verify karoQ8–Q9
PLA traceupdate sirf misclassification pe: positive galat → $w \leftarrow w + x$, negative galat → $w \leftarrow w - x$; sab points sahi = convergedQ10–Q11
Forward + backprop (CE)$h_i = \sigma(w_i x + b_i)$ → $\hat{y} = \sigma(\sum v_i h_i + b)$; CE ke saath $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w_1} = (\hat{y}-y)\,v_1\,h_1(1-h_1)\,x$Q12–Q13
Momentum update$u_t = \beta u_{t-1} + \nabla w_t$, phir $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta u_t$; mini-batch gradient $= \frac{1}{B}\sum (\hat{y}_i - y_i)x_i$Q14–Q15

Q2 · 1 markTrue/FalseDecision Boundary

"Neural network dwara seekha gaya decision boundary hamesha non-linear hota hai."

  • a. True
  • ✓b. False
Solution kholo
  1. Single perceptron / sigmoid neuron / linear network ki boundary $w^Tx + b = 0$ — linear!
  2. Non-linearity hidden layers ke non-linear activations se aati hai — "always" ka word galat banata hai.

Answer: False

Q3 · 2 marksMCQMP Quantifiers

Statement I: "Ek single MP neuron saare linearly separable boolean functions represent kar sakta hai." Statement II: "Har linearly separable boolean function kam se kam ek MP neuron se represent ho sakta hai."

  • a. Sirf Statement I true
  • ✓b. Sirf Statement II true
  • c. Dono true
  • d. Koi nahi
Solution kholo
  1. Statement I me quantifier hai "ek single neuron — saare functions" — ek fixed neuron to sirf ek function realize karta hai (ek threshold choice) → FALSE.
  2. Statement II sirf existence per function bolta hai: har linearly separable function ke liye koi na koi MP neuron exist karta hai → TRUE (standard MP representability result).
  3. Ye question quantifiers ("a single" vs "there exists") ka trap hai — dhyan se padho!

Answer: b

Q4 · 2 marksMCQGD Learning Rate

$L(w) = w^2$ pe same starting point ($w_0 = 2$) se do GD runs: Graph X — monotone decay, ~5 steps me zero. Graph Y — loss grow hoke 200+ cross kar raha hai (divergence). Kaunsa option sahi ho sakta hai?

  • a. X: $\eta = 1.1$, Y: $\eta = 0.3$
  • ✓b. X: $\eta = 0.3$, Y: $\eta = 1.1$
Solution kholo
  1. $\nabla L = 2w$ → $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta(2w_t) = (1-2\eta)w_t$ — geometric series!
  2. $\eta = 0.3$: multiplier $0.4$ → $w_t = 0.4^t\cdot2$, loss $= 4(0.16)^t$ → ~5 steps me zero → Graph X ✓
  3. $\eta = 1.1$: multiplier $-1.2$, $|-1.2| \gt 1$ → $w_t = (-1.2)^t\cdot2$, loss $4(1.44)^t$ → explode → Graph Y ✓
  4. Stability condition yaad rakho: quadratic pe convergence ke liye $|1-2\eta| \lt 1$, yaani $0 \lt \eta \lt 1$.

Answer: b

Q5 · 2 marksMCQMomentum Curve Matching

$L(w) = (w-5)^2$, $w_0 = -5$, $\eta = 0.04$, char methods: Vanilla GD ($\beta=0$) aur momentum ($\beta \in \{0.5, 0.9, 0.99\}$). Curves: S = smooth monotone decay (~40 steps me 0); T = fastest, ~10 steps me 0; U = fast drop + chhota bump (step ~20 pe), phir settle; V = bade decaying oscillations, 150 steps tak converge nahi.

  • ✓a. S: $\beta=0$, T: $\beta=0.5$, U: $\beta=0.9$, V: $\beta=0.99$
  • b. S: $\beta=0.99$, T: $\beta=0.9$, U: $\beta=0.5$, V: $\beta=0$
  • c. S: $\beta=0.5$, T: $\beta=0$, U: $\beta=0.99$, V: $\beta=0.9$
  • d. S: $\beta=0$, T: $\beta=0.9$, U: $\beta=0.5$, V: $\beta=0.99$
Solution kholo
  1. Momentum ka effective step size ~$\eta/(1-\beta)$ hota hai: $\beta = 0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99$ → effective $0.04, 0.08, 0.4, 4$.
  2. $\beta=0$: plain GD — slow, smooth, monotone → S
  3. $\beta=0.5$: halki inertia — fastest clean convergence → T
  4. $\beta=0.9$: zyada inertia — overshoot ka chhota bump → U
  5. $\beta=0.99$: bahut zyada inertia — bade lambe oscillations, converge nahi → V
  6. Rule yaad rakho: β badhne par speed badhlti hai, par oscillation/overshoot bhi badhta hai.

Answer: a

Q6 · 3 marksMCQPLA Angle

PLA: current $w = [3, 4]^T$. Misclassified example $x = [4, 3]^T$, label $y = -1$. Update: $w_{new} = w + \eta yx$ ($\eta = 1$). $w_{new}$ aur $x$ ke beech ka angle $\theta_{new}$ kya hai?

  • a. $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{5\sqrt{2}}\right)$
  • b. $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}\right)$
  • ✓c. $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{5\sqrt{2}}\right)$
  • d. $0°$
Solution kholo
  1. Update: $w_{new} = [3,4]^T + (1)(-1)[4,3]^T = [3-4, 4-3]^T = [-1, 1]^T$
  2. $\cos\theta_{new} = \frac{w_{new}^Tx}{\|w_{new}\|\|x\|} = \frac{(-1)(4) + (1)(3)}{\sqrt{2}\cdot 5} = \frac{-1}{5\sqrt{2}}$
  3. $\theta_{new} = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{5\sqrt{2}}\right) \approx 98.13°$
  4. Geometric sanity: negative point ke liye update $w$ ko $x$ se door ghumata hai — angle $90°$ se upar gaya → negative cosine ✓ (Ye Week 1 ka core geometry hai!)

Answer: c

Q7 · 3 marksMultiple SelectTraining Truths

Neural network training ke baare me kaunse statements TRUE hain?

  • a. SGD (batch size $B=1$) har step pe total loss ka true gradient compute karta hai
  • ✓b. Mini-batch GD ($B$, $N$ points) me 1 epoch = $\lceil N/B \rceil$ updates
  • ✓c. Momentum GD narrow valley ko overshoot kar sakta hai (accumulated velocity se)
  • ✓d. Vanilla GD me smooth loss + sufficiently small η pe har step loss ghatata hai (guaranteed)
Solution kholo
  1. (a) ✗ — B=1 pe gradient ek hi example ka hota hai — noisy estimate, true gradient nahi.
  2. (b) ✓ — $N$ points, batches of $B$ → $\lceil N/B \rceil$ updates per epoch.
  3. (c) ✓ — velocity minimum ke paar le ja sakti hai (Fig 4.1 wala behaviour).
  4. (d) ✓ — smooth $L$ + chhota η: $L(w-\eta\nabla L) \approx L - \eta\|\nabla L\|^2 \lt L$ (local descent lemma).

Answer: b, c, d

Q8 · 3 marksMultiple SelectIdentical Weights

Hidden layer ke $n$ neurons — sab identical weights $w$ aur identical bias $b$ se initialized. Activation = sigmoid. Kaunse statements TRUE hain?

  • a. Ek GD step ke baad neurons ke weights alag ho jayenge
  • ✓b. Kisi bhi input $x$ ke liye saare neurons same output denge
  • c. Backprop me sab neurons ke gradients hamesha zero hote hain (identical weights ki wajah se)
  • ✓d. Ye layer functionally single neuron ke equivalent hai
Solution kholo
  1. Identical init → identical pre-activations $\sigma(w^Tx + b)$ → identical outputs → (b) ✓
  2. Gradients bhi identical hote hain — par zero nahi (c ✗). Symmetric updates weights ko hamesha identical rakhte hain.
  3. Layer kabhi differentiate nahi ho sakti → effectively 1 neuron → (d) ✓, (a) ✗.
  4. Lesson: isi symmetry problem ki wajah se weights ko randomly initialize karte hain!

Answer: b, d

Q9 · 3 marksMultiple SelectMP + Inhibitory

MP neuron: 3 inputs. $x_1, x_2$ excitatory; $x_3$ inhibitory. Threshold = 2. Fires iff: inhibitory inactive AND excitatory sum ≥ threshold. Kaunse statements correct hain?

  • ✓a. $(1,1,0)$ input pe output 1
  • b. $(1,1,1)$ input pe output 1
  • ✓c. $(1,0,0)$ input pe output 0
  • d. Threshold 2 → 3 karne se kisi bhi input ka output change nahi hoga
Solution kholo
  1. Firing rule: $x_3 = 0$ AND $x_1 + x_2 \ge 2$.
  2. (a): $x_3=0$, sum $= 2 \ge 2$ → fires ✓ TRUE
  3. (b): $x_3 = 1$ inhibitory active → output 0, not 1 ✗
  4. (c): sum $= 1 \lt 2$ → output 0 ✓ TRUE
  5. (d): threshold 3 pe $(1,1,0)$ flip ho jayega (1 → 0) ✗

Answer: a, c

Q10 · 4 marksMultiple SelectPLA Trace + Bias

Perceptron: $w = [2,-1]^T$, $b = 0$. Predict $+1$ iff $w^Tx + b \ge 0$, else $-1$. Misclassification pe: $w \leftarrow w + y_ix_i$, $b \leftarrow b + y_i$. Order: A(3,1,+1) → B(2,0,−1) → C(1,2,−1) → D(4,4,+1).

  • ✓a. Pehla update point B ke baad hota hai
  • b. Dusra update point C ke baad hota hai
  • c. Final bias $= -1$
  • ✓d. Exactly do weight updates hote hain
Solution kholo
  1. A (3,1,+1): $w^Tx + b = 6-1 = 5 \ge 0$ → $+1$ = label ✓ no update
  2. B (2,0,−1): $= 4 \ge 0$ → predicted $+1 \ne -1$ ✗ → update #1: $w = (2,-1)-(2,0) = (0,-1)$, $b = -1$
  3. C (1,2,−1): $= 0-2-1 = -3 \lt 0$ → predicted $-1$ = label ✓ no update
  4. D (4,4,+1): $= 0-4-1 = -5 \lt 0$ → predicted $-1 \ne +1$ ✗ → update #2: $w = (0,-1)+(4,4) = (4,3)$, $b = -1+1 = 0$
  5. Total: 2 updates — pehla B ke baad, dusra D ke baad (C nahi!). Final $b = 0$.

Answer: a, d

Q11 · 4 marksMultiple SelectPerceptron vs Sigmoid

Perceptrons aur sigmoid neurons ke regarding kaunse statements correct hain?

  • ✓a. Perceptron threshold cross pe abruptly change hota hai; sigmoid smoothly
  • ✓b. Sigmoid differentiable hai → gradient-based learning ke liye suitable
  • ✓c. Sufficiently bade weights se sigmoid ≈ perceptron ka output
  • ✓d. Single hidden layer wala perceptron network koi bhi Boolean function exactly represent karta hai
  • ✓e. Single hidden layer wala sigmoid network koi bhi continuous function desired precision tak approximate karta hai
  • f. Single sigmoid neuron $\mathbb{R}^n$ ki har non-linear decision boundary represent kar sakta hai
Solution kholo
  1. (a) ✓ step vs smooth — Week 2 ka pehla concept.
  2. (b) ✓ $\sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)(1-\sigma(z))$ exists everywhere.
  3. (c) ✓ $w$ bada karo → sigmoid sharp hoti hai → step jaisi (tower trick ka base!).
  4. (d) ✓ Week 1 ka MLP theorem (2ⁿ construction).
  5. (e) ✓ Universal approximation theorem (Cybenko/Hornik).
  6. (f) ✗ single sigmoid neuron ka $0.5$-level set hyperplane hai — sirf linear boundaries.

Answer: a, b, c, d, e

Q12 · 4 marksMultiple SelectSigmoid Taylor

$\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1+e^{-z}}$ ke Taylor approximation pe kaunse statements true hain?

  • ✓a. First-order Taylor ($e^{-z} \approx 1-z$) se $z=0$ ke paas $\sigma(z) \approx \frac{1}{2} + \frac{z}{4}$
  • ✓b. $\sigma'(0) = \frac{1}{4}$
  • c. First-order Taylor se sigmoid saare $z$ ke liye exactly linear ho jata hai
  • ✓d. $|z|$ bahut bada hone par linear approximation increasingly inaccurate hota hai
  • ✓e. Sigmoid ki smooth differentiability gradient-based learning enable karti hai — hard-threshold perceptron ke ulat
Solution kholo
  1. (a): $\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1+e^{-z}} \approx \frac{1}{1+(1-z)} = \frac{1}{2-z} \approx \frac{1}{2}\left(1+\frac{z}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}+\frac{z}{4}$ ✓
  2. (b): $\sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)(1-\sigma(z))$ → $\sigma'(0) = \frac12\cdot\frac12 = \frac14$ ✓ (slope (a) se match!)
  3. (c) ✗ Taylor local approximation hai — exactly linear kabhi nahi.
  4. (d) ✓ expansion $z=0$ ke around hai.
    Bade $|z|$ pe $\sigma \to 0/1$ jabki $\frac12+\frac{z}{4}$ diverge karta hai.
  5. (e) ✓ derivatives → gradients → GD possible.
    Step function ka gradient almost everywhere 0.

Answer: a, b, d, e

Q13 · 3 marksShort AnswerZero-Weights Forward Pass

House price prediction: input $h_0 = [x_1, x_2]^T$ (quality, living area) → hidden layer 3 sigmoid neurons ($W_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{3\times2}, b_1$) → output 1 linear neuron ($W_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{1\times3}, b_2$). Init: $W_1 = 0$, $W_2 = 100$, biases $= 0$. House: quality $= 8$, area $= 3000$ sq.ft. Initial network ka predicted price?

Solution kholo
  1. $a_1 = W_1x + b_1 = [0,0,0]^T$ (saare first-layer weights/biases zero)
  2. Har hidden neuron: $\sigma(0) = 0.5$ — input se completely independent! (8 aur 3000 ki koi value kuch nahi badalti)
  3. Output: $\hat{y} = W_2h_1 + b_2 = 100(0.5 + 0.5 + 0.5) + 0 = 100 \times 1.5 = 150$

Answer: 150 — lesson: zero first-layer weights → hidden layer dead → output input-independent

Q14 · 3 marksShort AnswerSoftmax Inverse

3-class softmax, pre-activations $a = [a_1, 0, 0]$. Class 1 ki predicted probability exactly $\hat{y}_1 = 0.5$ hone ke liye $a_1$ kya ho? (2 decimal)

Solution kholo
  1. $\hat{y}_1 = \frac{e^{a_1}}{e^{a_1} + e^0 + e^0} = \frac{e^{a_1}}{e^{a_1}+2}$
  2. $\frac{e^{a_1}}{e^{a_1}+2} = 0.5$ → $e^{a_1} = 2$ → $a_1 = \ln 2 \approx 0.6931$
  3. 2 decimal: $0.69$ (official range 0.67–0.71 ✓)

Answer: 0.69 (= ln 2)

Q15 · 3 marksShort AnswerSigmoid ∂L/∂w

Sigmoid neuron $f(x) = \frac{1}{1+e^{-(wx+b)}}$. Training example $(x, y) = (2, 0.8)$; $w = 0$, $b = 0$. Loss $L = \frac{1}{2}(f(x)-y)^2$. $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w}$ nikalo. (2 decimal)

Solution kholo
  1. $f(x) = \sigma(0) = 0.5$
  2. Chain rule (Week 2 ka derived formula!): $\frac{\partial L}{\partial w} = (f(x)-y)\cdot f(x)(1-f(x))\cdot x$
  3. $= (0.5 - 0.8)(0.5)(0.5)(2) = (-0.3)(0.25)(2) = -0.15$ ✓ (range −0.17 to −0.13)

Answer: −0.15

Q16–Q17 · ComprehensionIdentity Activations6 marks

Shared data: 10-category classifier: Input (50 features) → Hidden 1 (64 sigmoid) → Hidden 2 (32 sigmoid) → Output (10 softmax), cross-entropy loss $-\log\hat{y}_\ell$. Chain: $a_1 = W_1x+b_1$, $h_1 = \sigma(a_1)$; $a_2 = W_2h_1+b_2$, $h_2 = \sigma(a_2)$; $a_3 = W_3h_2+b_3$, $\hat{y} = \text{softmax}(a_3)$.

Q16 (3 marks): Ab hidden layers me identity function ($h_i = a_i$) use karo (softmax output same). Kaunsa TRUE?
Options: (a) softmax non-linear hai isliye non-linear boundaries seekh lega · (b) Network ek single softmax regression $\hat{y} = O(W'x + b')$ ke equivalent hai, $W' = W_3W_2W_1$ · (c) Training fail ho jayegi (gradients linear layers se flow nahi kar sakte) · (d) Training $W_1, W_2, W_3$ ko identity matrices pe converge karwa degi
Q17 (3 marks): Training example pe true class $\ell$ ke liye $\hat{y}_\ell = 0.99$. $\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial a_{L,\ell}}$? (2 decimal)

  • ✓Q16: (b) — equivalent to softmax regression
  • ✓Q17: $-0.01$
Solution kholo
  1. Q16: Identity activations se: $a_3 = W_3(W_2(W_1x+b_1)+b_2)+b_3 = (W_3W_2W_1)x + \underbrace{(W_3W_2b_1 + W_3b_2 + b_3)}_{b'}$ — poora network ek affine map + softmax = softmax regression → (b) ✓
  2. (a) ✗ softmax affine input pe lag raha hai — boundaries linear hi rehti hain. (c) ✗ linear layers se gradients perfectly flow karte hain (bas collapse ho jate hain). (d) ✗ training ko identity matrices pe jaane ki koi wajah nahi — product hi matter karta hai.
  3. Q17: Softmax + CE ka shortcut (Week 3!): $\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial a_{L,j}} = \hat{y}_j - \mathbb{1}[j=\ell]$
  4. True class ke liye: $\hat{y}_\ell - 1 = 0.99 - 1 = -0.01$ ✓ (range −0.03–0.01)

Answer: Q16: b · Q17: −0.01

Q18–Q19 · ComprehensionUpdates Per Epoch4 marks

Shared data: 200 bird species classifier, dataset = 100,000 audio clips. Vanilla GD se start kiya.
Q18 (2 marks): Vanilla GD me per epoch kitne parameter updates?
Q19 (2 marks): Mini-batch GD me batch size $B = 50$ — per epoch kitne updates?

  • ✓Q18: 1
  • ✓Q19: 2000
Solution kholo
  1. Q18: Vanilla GD poore dataset ka gradient ek baar banata hai → 1 update per epoch — chahe 100,000 points hon!
  2. Q19: $N/B = 100000/50 = \mathbf{2000}$ updates per epoch.

Answer: Q18: 1 · Q19: 2000
